newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Hardie eyes Japanese building market.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Hardie eyes Japanese building market.

text.p: Australian building materials group James Hardie Industries Ltd said on Wednesday it sees Japan as the second most attractive market after the United States to sell its fibre cement product.
Managing director Keith Barton told a briefing at the Securities Institute of Australia that the group had just completed a study on Europe and Asia to assess opportunities.
"But none of those markets will be as attractive as the U.S. market due to the nature of the construction there, but the second market to the U.S we see is Japan," Barton said.
"But the question is, how do you get into Japan," he added.
James Hardie said earlier on Wednesday that it planned to build a fourth fibre cement plant in the United States.
Barton said the company was currently exporting about 30 percent of its Australian fibre cement production and that he expected the group to be exporting to the U.S. for another 12 months.
He said earnings before interest and tax from the U.S. operations was growing faster than revenue.
"It won't be too long before the U.S. is half our profits," he said. James Hardie earlier said it expected lower profits for the six months to September 30, and the full 1996/97 year.
James Hardie reported a net profit of A$32.2 million in the year to March 31, 1996, compared with A$74.6 million in 1994/95.
Barton said the next Asian expansion would be in the Philippines where the company has been looking to build a plant for fibre cement production.
"We are about to go global and open plants around the world, but we are carefully studying opportunities and we will prioritise them and we will be quite selective," Barton said.
The shares ended three cents lower at A$3.40, on a day when the overall market was higher.
